name: Ecological trajectory analysis (ecotraj)
title: Is a share path drifting on purpose, or just wandering?
what: Treat each period's mix as a point; measure whether the path keeps one direction, and split market from firm-specific moves.
pick_line: Port and speed done; math split passes; power curve running; new-use rerun on repo data.
data: Public FR Y-9C proxy, public OFR repo aggregates, and simulations; descriptive only
one: Increment split finds planted drifts 99.7% of the time; on repo collateral mix it narrowly misses.

left.sub: of planted sticky swaps found at T = 62 (it hides them)

right.sub: found, with a 5.3% false-alarm rate when there is none

findings.h: Math (Extension 2): the increment split has the right size and real power.
findings.t: Pre-registered simulation, 2,000 runs per cell: false alarms 5.2% (T = 40) and 5.3% (T = 62); planted swap found 93.7% and 99.7%. The old level split: 0.1% and 1.3%.

findings.h: Engineering (Extension 1): a Python port at R parity, 160× faster than R.
findings.t: 1,260 of 1,280 randomized checks match ecotraj 1.2.2 exactly; the other 20 are R floating-point quirks on exactly collinear points. 999 sign-flip draws on 62 × 14: 98.8 s in R, 0.59 s on one core.

chart.title: Seconds for 999 null draws, T = 62 × 14 parts

findings.note: 160× = 98.8 / 0.593, computed. R time extrapolated from warm batches (ecotraj-py bench).

findings.h: New use (11-17): on repo collateral mix, a directional residual drift that does not survive Holm.
findings.t: Market = VIX, 10-year yield, total volume. Tri-party collateral mix: residual directionality 0.628, p = 0.036 (Holm 0.072). Venue × tenor mix: 0.560, p = 0.164. Pre-set bar: Holm p ≤ 0.05 on either.
findings.note: Residual drift in collateral: corporate debt up (+1.09 clr), Treasury down (−0.83). The 11-12 row is the scout's proxy panel, for scale.

findings.h: P2 (11-17): it reliably sees swaps of 0.075 per step or more; smaller ones are mostly missed.
findings.t: Pre-registered power curve, 1,000 runs per cell. The size check passes (6 parts: 0.051 and 0.042, band 0.03–0.07). At T = 62 the smallest swap with ≥ 80% power is 0.075 with 14 parts and 0.10 with 6 parts. A 0.05 swap is caught 50% of the time with 14 parts and 28% with 6.
findings.note: Source: jgridifier/ecotraj-py results/P2_RESULTS.md (PR #12); pre-registration prereg/P2_PREREG.md (PR #11, merged before the run). Synthetic data.
